Proposed Int. No. 211-A Fiscal Impact Statement - City Council

Summary: This bill would require the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) to conduct a public education and outreach campaign by December 1, 2027 on fertility treatment services, including information about insurance coverage, Medicaid coverage, and information about benefits administered or provided by New York City or New York State that may assist individuals in accessing fertility treatment services. The campaign would be conducted via internet, subway and other public transportation advertisements, and LinkNYC kiosks. Campaign information would be made available in physical and digital formats at DOHMH facilities, and would be provided to public hospitals, federally qualified health centers, health care providers, and clinics citywide. These materials would also be posted on the DOHMH website. Beginning by December 1, 2028, DOHMH would be required annually to provide campaign materials to health care providers for distribution to the public.

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:\ulnone\par
\pard\ltrpar\fi720\qj\par
\pard\ltrpar\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj Section 1. Section 17-199.19 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by local law number 88 for the year 2022, is amended to read as follows:\par
\cf1\'a7 17-199.19 Provision of sexual and reproductive health services. a. \cf0 The department shall provide \cf1 sexual and reproductive health services and \cf0 conduct \cf1 research on sexual and reproductive health disparities within the city. In providing such services, the department shall have the power and duty to:\par
1. Provide outreach, education, and support to individuals, especially low-income individuals and those without health insurance, regarding issues related to sexual and reproductive health, including, but not limited to:\par
(a) Contraception, including a broad range of methods such as long-acting reversible contraception;\par
(b) Preconception health services;\par
(c) Abortion services;\par
(d) Family planning services;\par
(e) Testing, prevention, and treatment for HIV;\par
(f) Testing and treatment for sexually transmitted infections;\par
\pard\cbpat3\ltrpar\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj\cf2 (g) Routine screening for breast and cervical cancer; and\par
(h) Health education, in community settings, to promote reproductive health, prevent unintended pregnancy, and promote access to reproductive and preventive health services.\ul\par
\pard\ltrpar\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj\cf1\ulnone 2. Make referrals, when determined appropriate by the department, to affordable and accessible services related to contraception; abortion; family planning; breast and cervical cancer screenings; and counseling, testing, and treatment for HIV and sexually transmitted infections.\par
\ul 3. No later than December 1, 2027, in collaboration with any relevant agency designated by the mayor, create and implement a public education and outreach campaign about fertility treatment and \cf0 insurance coverage of fertility treatment services\cf1 . Such campaign shall, at minimum, be conducted via internet, subway and other public transportation advertisements, and LinkNYC kiosks. Such information shall be made available in physical and digital formats at facilities operated by the department, and shall be provided to public hospitals, federally qualified health centers, \cf0 health care providers,\cf1  and clinics citywide. \cf0 Such campaign shall provide the following information:\par
(a) The different types of fertility treatment, including, but not limited to, in vitro fertilization and fertility preservation treatment;\par
(b) How fertility treatment can be an important part of comprehensive healthcare;\par
(c) Factors that may affect fertility and fertility treatment outcomes, including age, and considerations for when to seek fertility care;\par
(d) Fertility treatment insurance coverage requirements for individual, small group, and large group comprehensive health insurance policies as set forth in the New York insurance law;\par
(e) Eligibility criteria under Medicaid in New York state for coverage of fertility treatment; \par
(f) Information about benefits administered or provided by New York state or the city that may assist individuals in accessing fertility treatment services, including, but not limited to, the infertility reimbursement program administered by the New York state department of health; and\par
(g) Fertility treatment services required to be covered under Medicaid in New York state.\par
4. Annual outreach. No later than December 1, 2028, and annually thereafter, the department shall conduct public outreach on the campaign developed and implemented pursuant to paragraph 3 of this subdivision. Such outreach shall include, at minimum, the distribution of materials created pursuant to such paragraph to \cf1 public hospitals, federally qualified health centers, \cf0 health care providers,\cf1  and clinics citywide for distribution to the public.\cf0\par
\cf1 b. Materials. No later than December 1, 2027, the department shall post and maintain the materials used for outreach and education required under paragraphs 1 and 3 of subdivision a of this section on the department\rquote s website in the designated citywide languages, as defined in section 23-1101.\par
\pard\ltrpar\qj\cf0\ulnone\'a7 2. \cf1 This local law takes effect immediately. \cf0\fs18\par
